body:
Hi,
You can use [self_group](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/sqlelement.html#sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnElement.self_group) to ensure parenthesis are used.

self_group is likely what's broken here.

For the moment work around as:

```
from sqlalchemy.sql.elements import Grouping
expr = Grouping(type_coerce(...))
```

here's a test case that shows where this should be consistent:

```
from sqlalchemy import column, type_coerce, Integer, cast


a = column("a") / (column("b") * column("c"))
b = column("a") / cast(column("b") * column("c"), Integer)
c = column("a") / type_coerce(column("b") * column("c"), Integer)


print(a)
print(b)
print(c)
```

proposed fix, needs to defer to the inner expression for correct grouped behavior:

```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py
index 43115f117..059b054d4 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/elements.py
@@ -2893,6 +2893,12 @@ class TypeCoerce(WrapsColumnExpression, ColumnElement):
     def wrapped_column_expression(self):
         return self.clause
 
+    def self_group(self, against=None):
+        grouped = self.clause.self_group(against=against)
+        if grouped is not self.clause:
+            return TypeCoerce(grouped, self.type)
+        else:
+            return self
 
 class Extract(ColumnElement):
     """Represent a SQL EXTRACT clause, ``extract(field FROM expr)``."""

```
I'll look into this, since the documentation could also be improved for type_coerce, since it's not super clear why one should use it

The documentation is not correct regarding the `anon_1` label:
```py
stmt = select([
                type_coerce(log_table.date_string, StringDateTime())
            ])
```
now renders 
```sql
SELECT date_string AS date_string FROM log
```
not `anon_1` as stated in the docs

Edit: only in master, 1_3 still has anon_1

Interestingly 
```py
stmt = select([
                type_coerce(log_table.date_string, StringDateTime())
                type_coerce(log_table.date_string, Time())
            ])
```
renders
```sql
SELECT date_string AS date_string, date_string AS date_string FROM log
```
but the processing happens correctly
yeah those anon_1 / label things change quite often, if you don't set an explicit label it's not defined what the format of an anonymous label will be so this is not critical

**Federico Caselli** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Correctly apply self_group in type_coerce element.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1998

**Federico Caselli** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Correctly apply self_group in type_coerce element.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1999

issue.title: SQLite and Postgresql have conflicting operator precedence for the string concat and math operators

labels.name: question
labels.description: issue where a "fix" on the SQLAlchemy side is unlikely, hence more of a usage question

labels.name: datatypes
labels.description: things to do with database types, like VARCHAR and others

labels.name: use case

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
SQLAlchemy (on the latest master version) does not place correct parenthesis when using the `||` operator.

**Expected behavior**
```python
expr = type_coerce(Author.id + literal(1), types.String)
f = (Author.first_name + expr).label('f')
session.query(f).select_from(Author)
```

I expect the following query:

```sql
SELECT author.first_name || (author.id + ?) AS f
FROM author
```

Producing:

```
Name1
Name2
...
```

Instead SQLAlchemy generate the following query:

```sql
SELECT author.first_name || author.id + ? AS f
FROM author
```

Leading to incorrect results:

```
1
1
...
```

Unlike the SQL operator `+`, the operator `||` has the highest precedence.
Therefore to interpret this query correctly parenthesis are needed.
For more details see [here](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html#operators)

**Versions.**
SQLAlchemy latest master version([commit](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/3b2c6692bd5df6fe4a37192dfdaed408e3be5e54))

**Have a nice day!**
